sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a house in Amarillo?
sections.html:
Sell through an agent if the house is in good shape and you can wait for a financed buyer, or sell for cash if speed, repairs or a tenant make a traditional listing hard. Amarillo is the commercial center of the Texas Panhandle, and mid-2025 estimates count 205,130 residents.

Amarillo is large, and it sits in two counties, so the first step is to find out which county your house is in. The city lies mostly in Potter County and extends into Randall County, which means the tax office, the clerk and the appraisal records you deal with depend on the parcel.

  • Look up the address with the Potter Randall Appraisal District, which determines ownership for both counties.
  • Call the tax office named on your tax statement early in the process.
  • Ask the City of Amarillo's Building Safety office about any open permits on the property.

sections.h2: What does Amarillo's housing market look like in Census data?
sections.html:
Amarillo is an affordable Texas city, with a median home value under $200,000 and about four in ten households renting. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table shows the figures below, and the city's 2020 population count was 200,393, compared with 190,695 in 2010.

A mean commute of 19.6 minutes is short for a city of 102 square miles. The Census Bureau also counts 10,973 veterans in the 2020-2024 estimates, so disabled veteran exemptions are worth asking about when you sell or buy.

sections.h2: How did Amarillo develop, and what does it mean for homes today?
sections.html:
Amarillo was platted in April 1887 along the Fort Worth and Denver City Railway in Potter County and named for a nearby lake and creek, probably after the yellow soil or spring wildflowers. The Texas State Historical Association says the first site was on low ground that would flood, so a rancher and his partner bought land to the east in 1888 and drew merchants to higher ground. By 1890 the town's center had moved a mile east, and the county seat followed in 1893.

The economy grew from cattle shipping into wheat, gas, oil and helium. Gas was discovered in 1918 and oil in 1921, and the Cliffside field's helium led to a federal helium plant in 1928. In World War II Amarillo hosted an Army Air Field and the nearby Pantex plant, and the city's population hit 51,686 by 1940. Interstate 40 and Interstate 27 later pulled new housing and shopping toward the south and west, according to the Handbook of Texas.

The same source describes a city that by 1980 had 149,230 residents and more than sixty square miles within Potter and Randall counties. Gas, petroleum, agriculture and cattle remain the entry's named income sources, and the Census data shows a large health care sector, with healthcare receipts of $2,777,390 thousand in 2022.

sections.h2: How do taxes work for a house in the Randall County part of Amarillo?
sections.html:
Randall County's tax office mails statements each October 1, and they are due on receipt. Paying by January 31 avoids penalty and interest, and February 1 starts delinquency. A payment sent by first-class mail counts as paid on the date of the post office cancellation mark.

The Randall County tax office also explains how a sale affects the bill:

  • The taxing unit does not prorate the year. Most sales contracts split the year's taxes between buyer and seller, so check the contract and closing statement.
  • Whoever owned the house on the first of January of the prior year remains liable for that year's tax, and the unit can also pursue the buyer through the lien.
  • Over-65, disabled and veteran homesteads can pay in four installments, with the first fourth and a signed agreement due by January 31. A first payment received by February 28 carries 7% penalty and interest, and a missed installment adds 6% penalty plus 1% interest each month.

A tax certificate shows delinquent taxes, penalties and interest for each taxing unit. The fee is $10, paid in certified funds at pickup, and you can request it by email and pick it up at either the Canyon or the Amarillo office. If taxes are due and you want a zero-balance certificate, pay with cash or certified funds or wait 10 working days for a check to clear.

The Potter Randall Appraisal District is at 5701 Hollywood Road, Amarillo, with a phone number of 806-358-1601 and a mailing address of P.O. Box 7190, Amarillo, TX 79114. For a parcel in Potter County, ask the Potter County tax assessor-collector for the same certificate.

sections.h2: Which Amarillo permit and platting rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Amarillo's Building Safety office is in the Simms Municipal Building at 808 S Buchanan Street, Suite 104, open weekdays from eight to five, and permits go through the MGO Connect online portal. The city's ordinance Sec. 4-10-21 says land cannot be used unless a Certificate of Occupancy and Compliance has been issued.

A Certificate of Occupancy is issued automatically for new buildings when the permit is completed. A separate certificate is needed when the use changes or when none was ever issued, and alterations require a remodel or repair permit with a registered contractor. For a house with a converted garage, a rented room or a business use, ask Building Safety whether the certificate matches what the house is today.

Platting matters if you want to sell part of a lot. The county's FAQ explains that a plat is required when land is divided for sale, and that in Amarillo it applies to any tract inside the city limits and to tracts of five acres or less in the extraterritorial jurisdiction extending five miles beyond the limits.

sections.h2: Does flood risk affect an Amarillo sale?
sections.html:
It can. The original town site was moved to higher ground after flooding concerns in 1888 and 1889, and drainage on the High Plains is still a buyer question. Randall County's floodplain page explains that a 100-year flood is a flood level with a 1% or greater chance of being equaled or exceeded in any year, not one that happens once a century.

  • You can request flood information from the county floodplain administrator by giving the Randall appraisal ID, the address and the legal description.
  • The Flood Insurance Rate Map shows special flood hazard areas, and a Letter of Map Amendment can remove a property that was mapped in by mistake.
  • Under the county's floodplain rules, improvements or repairs costing 50% or more of a building's market value count as substantial improvement or substantial damage.
  • Building without required county floodplain permits can bring fines up to $500 per day.

Lenders can require flood insurance independently of a map change, so a buyer's lender has the final say.

sections.h2: What if the Amarillo house is inherited, behind on payments or rented?
sections.html:
Texas gives owners a few timelines to work with, and Panhandle counties follow the same rules as the rest of the state.

  • Inherited: an heir not on the recorded deed must give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim the homestead exemption.
  • Behind on payments: lenders generally wait until a loan is more than 120 days late. A notice of sale must go out at least 21 days ahead of the first-Tuesday auction.
  • Tenants: written notice to vacate is at least three days unless the lease says otherwise. Eviction cases are filed in justice court, and a writ of possession is available six days after judgment.

Each of these paths can end in a sale, and the earlier you pick one, the more room you have.

faqs.q: Is Amarillo in Potter County or Randall County?
faqs.a: Both. The Handbook of Texas says the city is in southern Potter County and extends into Randall County, so a house's county depends on its parcel.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Randall County property tax?
faqs.a: On receipt. Pay by January 31 to avoid penalty and interest. Statements are mailed each October 1, and unpaid taxes are delinquent on February 1.

faqs.q: How much is a tax certificate in Randall County?
faqs.a: The fee is $10, paid with certified funds when you pick it up at the Canyon or Amarillo office. The certificate lists delinquent taxes for each taxing unit.

faqs.q: Does Amarillo require a Certificate of Occupancy?
faqs.a: Yes, under city ordinance Sec. 4-10-21. It is issued automatically for new buildings, and an existing property may need one if none was issued or the use changes.

faqs.q: What does a typical Amarillo owner-occupied home cost?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 median value for owner-occupied homes in Amarillo is $196,900.
